title: SQL injection in public /orders/search via 'customer' query parameter
evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:15-16 registers GET /orders/search with no auth decorator, and the docstring at :17 says the storefront's public order lookup page uses it. At :18 the `customer` value comes straight from request.args, with no validation. At :20 it is put into the SQL string with an f-string inside single quotes, and :21 runs it on a sqlite3 connection (app/db.py:8-11). A request like `?customer=' OR '1'='1` breaks out of the quotes and returns every order row (id, total, status) for every customer. UNION-based payloads can also read other tables. sqlite3's execute() runs only one statement, which limits stacked queries but doesn't stop data being read. An unauthenticated attacker can reach this route.
recommended_fix: Use a parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT id, total, status FROM orders WHERE customer_email = ?", (customer,)). Also think about whether a public endpoint should return orders based only on an email address. That is an authorization/enumeration issue on its own, even once the injection is fixed. Add a regression test that sends a quote payload.
